title: Agencies Request Comment on Proposals to Modernize the Regulatory Capital Framework and Maintain the Strength of the Banking System
summary: The FDIC, Federal Reserve Board, and OCC jointly requested public comment on three proposals to modernize bank regulatory capital requirements. The first proposal targets Category I and II banks and implements remaining Basel III components; the second adjusts capital requirements for banks engaged primarily in traditional lending; the third (Federal Reserve only) refines systemic risk measurement for G-SIBs. The agencies project modest capital reductions for large banks and moderate reductions for smaller institutions, while maintaining levels substantially above pre-financial crisis.
key_points: Three separate proposals: (1) Basel III completion for largest banks, (2) capital alignment for traditional lenders, (3) G-SIB systemic risk measurement reform
First proposal reduces dual-set calculation burden to single set for Category I and II banks; improves credit, market, and operational risk capture
Second proposal modifies mortgage servicing and origination capital requirements to reduce lending disincentives; applies to community bank leverage ratio framework banks
Third proposal from Federal Reserve Board only refines FR Y-15 systemic risk report for largest and most complex banks
Agencies project aggregate capital levels will modestly decrease but remain substantially higher than pre-crisis levels
why_it_matters: These proposals represent a significant modernization of U.S. bank capital rules. Changes could affect lending capacity, mortgage economics, and competitive dynamics between large and community banks. The first proposal streamlines calculation requirements for the largest banks while improving risk capture. The second proposal reduces disincentives for mortgage lending. The third proposal refines systemic risk measurement for the most complex institutions. Though not yet effective, market participants should monitor as final rules could alter bank profitability and risk-taking incentives over a multi-year implementation horizon.
macro_context: Capital requirements influence bank lending capacity and credit availability across the economy. Reduced requirements could support loan growth and economic activity over time. However, this is a request for comment rather than a final rule, with no immediate market impact. The agencies anticipate modest capital reductions while maintaining levels substantially above pre-crisis benchmarks.
market_structure_context: The proposals address regulatory capital framework architecture—specifically risk-based capital calculations, leverage ratio treatment, and systemic risk surcharges (FR Y-15). These rules determine how banks must hold capital against various asset classes and activities, affecting the competitive landscape between large complex banks and community banks. The first proposal consolidates dual-set calculations into a single set for Category I/II banks.
